Class ContributorTestbed

java.lang.Object
testCases.ContributorTestbed
public class ContributorTestbed extends Object

Title: ContributorTestbed Class

Description: Semi-automated tests showing that the LessonsLearned and LessonsLearnedList entity classes, and the Database methods that store them, satisfy the Contributor (Phase Two) user stories. It follows the pattern of the PasswordEvaluationTestbed: every test case has an ID, the requirement it checks, an expected result, and an actual result, and prints PASS or FAIL. A summary is printed at the end.

Organization: every test case is its own method, named after what it checks, with a Javadoc comment giving its test ID, its requirement, the user story text it comes from, the input, the expected result, and why a PASS shows the requirement is met. The test IDs (TC-C01 to TC-C46) and requirement IDs (R1 to R14) match the document "Contributor Test Plan - TP2". The manual tests in that plan are printed as a checklist at the end of the run and are performed through the Contributor GUI.

The Contributor user stories, numbered C1 to C4 in the order they appear in "Lessons Learned System V1":

  • C1: A contributor adds lessons with core information, sees and manages them, and cannot alter fields another role has locked or see what other roles added.
  • C2: A contributor sees a list of their own lessons, examines one, sees which fields are locked, and cannot delete a lesson that is locked or has a locked field.
  • C3: A contributor adds experience (time and effort) information to a lesson.
  • C4: A contributor sees only their own content, including a curator's edits of it, and never another contributor's submissions.

How results are judged: each test asks one question, "did the action succeed?" Positive tests use valid input and expect Success. Negative tests use bad input and expect Rejected. A test that throws an exception counts as FAIL and the exception is printed, so one broken method cannot stop the rest of the run.

Test groups:

  • Validation tests (R1, R2, R10) call LessonsLearned.validate(), which createLessonLearned() and updateLessonLearned() run before every save.
  • List tests (R8, R11, R14) build a LessonsLearnedList in memory.
  • Database tests (R1, R3 to R7, R10, R12 to R14) save and read lessons through the lessonLearnedDB table, using a separate test database.

Known failures: TC-C18, TC-C24, and TC-C25 fail because updateLessonLearned() and deleteLessonLearned() do not yet check locks, and TC-C44 fails because keyword search does not look at the keywords field. These tests are correct; they pass once the code is fixed.

  • Field Details

    • TEST_DB_URL

      private static final String TEST_DB_URL
      A separate H2 database used only by these tests.

      Source: Task 7 requires tests that can be run repeatedly without damaging data.

      Rationale: running against the real database would add test lessons to the application's data and could delete real lessons during cleanup.

      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • TEST_DB_IS_SAFE

      private static final boolean TEST_DB_IS_SAFE
      Safety switch for the database tests.

      Source: a bug found while writing these tests, where connectToDatabase() ignored the URL passed to Database(String) and always opened the real database.

      Rationale: the bug is fixed, so this is true. If it ever returns, setting this to false skips every database test instead of writing test lessons into real data.

      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • numPassed

      private static int numPassed
      The number of automated tests whose actual result matched the expected result.

      Source: the PasswordEvaluationTestbed pattern, which ends with a pass/fail count.

      Rationale: one total shows at a glance whether the requirements are met.

    • numFailed

      private static int numFailed
      The number of automated tests whose actual result did not match.

      Source: the PasswordEvaluationTestbed pattern.

      Rationale: any value above zero means a requirement is not yet met, or a test is wrong, and must be investigated before submission.

    • numPending

      private static int numPending
      The number of tests that cannot run yet.

      Source: the test plan includes tests for methods that do not exist yet.

      Rationale: counting them separately keeps them from being mistaken for passes or failures, and keeps them visible until they can run.

    • numManual

      private static int numManual
      The number of manual tests printed as a checklist.

      Source: Task 6 requires both semi-automated and manual tests.

      Rationale: some requirements are about what the screen shows and can only be checked by a person using the GUI; listing them here keeps every test in one run.

    • db

      private static database.Database db
      The test database connection used by the database tests.

      Source: the Database class from the Foundations code.

      Rationale: the tests call the same methods the application uses, so a PASS shows the application's own code works, not a copy of it.

    • createdIds

      private static List<Integer> createdIds
      The ids of the lessons the database tests create.

      Rationale: cleanUp() deletes exactly these lessons at the end of a run, so every run starts from the same state and nothing else in the test database is touched.

    • check

      private static void check(String id, String req, String description, boolean expected, BooleanSupplier test)

      Method: void check(String id, String req, String description, boolean expected, BooleanSupplier test)

      Description: Runs one automated test case and reports whether the actual result matched the expected result. This is the same report format as the PasswordEvaluationTestbed. An exception inside the test counts as a FAIL.

      Parameters:
      id - the test case ID, for example TC-C01
      req - the requirement the test case checks, for example R1
      description - what the test does, in plain words
      expected - true if the action should succeed, false if it should be rejected
      test - the code that performs the action and returns whether it succeeded

      Parameters:
      id - the test case ID
      req - the requirement the test case checks

      reason - why it cannot run yet

    • testBlankTitle

      private static void testBlankTitle()

      TC-C02 [R1, Negative]: Create a lesson with the title left blank.

      Story C1: "I can add new lessons learned to the system, specifying core information." The title is core information, so a lesson without one is incomplete.

      Expected: Rejected. A PASS shows validate() refuses a lesson with no title, so createLessonLearned() never saves one.

    • testSpacesOnlyTitle

      private static void testSpacesOnlyTitle()

      TC-C03 [R1, Negative]: Create a lesson whose title is only spaces.

      Story C1: core information is required. A title of spaces looks filled in on the screen but holds no information.

      Expected: Rejected. A PASS shows the setters trim the spaces, so the title counts as blank and is refused like TC-C02.

    • testBlankDescription

      private static void testBlankDescription()

      TC-C04 [R1, Negative]: Create a lesson with the description left blank.
